sub_unit_name: Knocking - Octane and Cetane Rating, Synthetic Petrol - Fischer-Tropsch Process

content.title: Knocking in Internal Combustion Engines
content.description: Knocking is an abnormal combustion phenomenon in which the unburnt fuel-air mixture explodes suddenly, producing a metallic knocking sound, reducing engine efficiency and causing damage.

content.content: Knocking is an undesirable phenomenon in both petrol and diesel engines. In petrol engines it occurs due to premature auto-ignition of the fuel-air mixture, whereas in diesel engines it is caused by excessive ignition delay before combustion.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Knocking reduces engine power, decreases fuel efficiency, increases fuel consumption, and shortens engine life.
Knocking in Petrol Engine

In a spark ignition (SI) engine, knocking occurs when the unburnt portion of the fuel-air mixture auto-ignites before the flame front reaches it, creating pressure waves that produce a knocking sound.

items.question: Power Loss
items.answer: Engine output decreases due to irregular combustion.

items.question: Engine Damage
items.answer: Continuous knocking damages pistons, valves, and cylinder walls.

items.question: Poor Fuel Economy
items.answer: More fuel is consumed for the same power output.

content.content: Octane Rating
Octane number measures the anti-knocking quality of petrol. A higher octane number indicates greater resistance to knocking and better engine performance.

content.title: Reference Fuels
content.content: Iso-octane has an octane number of 100 and n-heptane has an octane number of 0. Petrol is rated by comparing its knocking tendency with mixtures of these two fuels.
Importance of Octane Number

items.question: Better Combustion
items.answer: Ensures smooth combustion in petrol engines.

content.content: Knocking in Diesel Engine

In a compression ignition (CI) engine, knocking occurs due to excessive ignition delay. During this delay, more fuel accumulates in the combustion chamber and burns suddenly, producing a sharp knocking sound.
Cetane Rating
Cetane number indicates the ignition quality of diesel fuel. A higher cetane number means shorter ignition delay, smoother combustion, and less knocking.

content.title: Reference Fuels
content.content: Cetane (n-hexadecane) has a cetane number of 100, while α-methylnaphthalene is assigned a cetane number of 0.
Octane Number vs Cetane Number
Synthetic Petrol
Synthetic petrol is manufactured from coal, natural gas, or carbon monoxide and hydrogen instead of crude petroleum. It is produced to meet fuel demand when petroleum resources are limited.
Fischer-Tropsch Process

The Fischer-Tropsch process converts a mixture of carbon monoxide (CO) and hydrogen (H₂), called synthesis gas or water gas, into liquid hydrocarbons using a catalyst under controlled temperature and pressure.

content.title: Overall Reaction
content.code:
nCO + (2n + 1)H₂  →  CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ + nH₂O

Catalyst: Cobalt or Iron
Temperature: 200–300°C
Pressure: 5–25 atm

content.content: Advantages of Fischer-Tropsch Process

items.question: Alternative Fuel Source
items.answer: Produces petrol without depending on crude oil.

items.question: Cleaner Fuel
items.answer: Synthetic petrol contains fewer sulphur impurities.

items.question: Utilizes Coal
items.answer: Converts abundant coal resources into liquid fuels.

items.question: Industrial Importance
items.answer: Useful in countries with limited petroleum reserves.

content.content: Applications

items.question: Automobile Fuel
items.answer: Synthetic petrol is used in internal combustion engines.

items.question: Energy Security
items.answer: Reduces dependence on imported crude oil.

items.question: Chemical Industry
items.answer: Produces hydrocarbons used as petrochemical feedstock.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Knocking is abnormal combustion in IC engines.
Octane number measures anti-knocking quality of petrol.
Cetane number measures ignition quality of diesel.
Iso-octane = 100 and n-heptane = 0 for octane rating.
Cetane = 100 and α-methylnaphthalene = 0 for cetane rating.
Synthetic petrol is produced from synthesis gas.
Fischer-Tropsch process uses iron or cobalt catalyst.
Synthetic fuels reduce dependence on petroleum.
